evidence.summary: useState<string[] | null>(null); fetch(...).then(r => r.json()).then(setData); data === null ? null : data.map(...). There is no catch, explicit pending/empty/error output, retry, or status announcement.

findings.why_it_matters: Visitors cannot distinguish waiting, no projects and a failed request; assistive technology receives no state feedback.
findings.proposed_change: In a later authorized repair, model the real pending, success, empty and failure states, show proportional progress, announce feedback, and offer a safe retry.
findings.regression_risk: Keep /api/projects and real successful data behavior intact. Avoid fake success and decorative loading for synchronous content.

evidence.summary: fetch parses every response as JSON and forwards it to setData without checking r.ok or validating an array of strings; rendering calls data.map and inserts each item as a child.

findings.why_it_matters: An HTTP error body or malformed response can become a render exception instead of an honest recoverable error.
findings.proposed_change: Check HTTP status and validate the expected response before setting usable data; route failures into the frontend error state and preserve remote names as React text.
findings.regression_risk: Confirm the existing API response contract before adding validation; backend endpoints, payload semantics and authorization are outside this audit.

evidence.summary: <form><label>Email <input name="email" type="email" /></label><button>Join the list</button></form> has no action, method or onSubmit.

findings.why_it_matters: The claimed join action has no supplied subscription path or confirmation; default HTML GET submission can expose the email in the page URL. Actual submission is untested.
findings.proposed_change: Have the owner identify the real subscription contract before a scoped frontend integration; submit through that approved contract, validate input, and show honest pending/success/error feedback.
findings.regression_risk: Do not invent a subscription service or fake persistence. Preserve the valid implicit email label and native validation, and avoid putting personal data in query strings.

evidence.summary: Live demo provides a placeholder fragment rather than a demo.
BRIEF.md: no live demonstration URL has been supplied.

findings.why_it_matters: The label promises a demonstration that this source cannot open.
findings.proposed_change: Obtain a working authentic demo URL or owner-approved accurate preview wording before changing this claim.
findings.regression_risk: Do not fabricate product UI or footage, invent a destination, or delete a genuine claim without agreement.

evidence.summary: BRIEF.md explicitly says the testimonial provenance is unknown.

findings.why_it_matters: A quantified endorsement with unknown provenance can mislead readers; this audit cannot determine whether the statement is true.
findings.proposed_change: Request the original quote, attribution permission and basis for the revenue claim from the owner. Decide whether to keep, accurately label or remove it only with the owner.
findings.regression_risk: Unknown does not mean fake. Preserve the source during this audit and never invent a substitute quote, reviewer or metric.
